input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 matches the preferred position exactly: we may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience (in whole or in part) on thirty days' written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination fee, and Copperleaf is expressly denied any convenience-termination right during a committed term. No other provision grants the Vendor a convenience right (§§ 9.1–9.3 are breach/insolvency/cause based, and § 24.4 blocks change-of-control termination). Section 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" is in tension with the economics of § 9.4, but that is a minimum-commitment issue to be raised under MINCOMMIT rather than double-flagged here. Clause is favourable to us; no redline.
